answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require dynamic collateral bonding, where each identity locks escrowed capital subject to automated slashing for Byzantine behavior. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce liquid funds per identity, forming a basalt floor of capital expenditure that stops a fleeting zephyr of synthetic nodes from cheaply capturing consensus. However, locking liquidity prices out underfunded honest agents, stranding them on an economic island.
